key_insight: Chameleon introduces an episodic memory that stores rich, fine‑grained perceptual traces and retrieves decision‑relevant past experiences to disambiguate perceptually aliased observations, enabling more reliable long‑horizon robotic manipulation.
problem_solved: Perceptual aliasing and occlusions make single observations ambiguous during long tasks; existing compressed memory/retrieval schemes lose disambiguating cues and return irrelevant episodes, causing failures in multi-step manipulation.
method: Store rich episodic traces (temporal snippets of observations, actions, and outcomes) instead of heavily compressed semantic summaries to preserve disambiguating perceptual details.
Learn a retrieval mechanism that prioritizes decision‑relevant cues (not just perceptual similarity) to fetch past episodes that clarify current ambiguous observations.
Integrate retrieved episodic context with the policy/controller so action selection uses both current observation and relevant episodic history to resolve non‑Markovian decisions.
impact: Provides a practical way to handle non‑Markovian decision problems in embodied agents, improving robustness to occlusion and state changes in long‑horizon robotic tasks. This approach can be incorporated into manipulation stacks to reduce failure rates and enable more complex multi‑step behaviors.
visual_elements: Before vs after scenario: two side‑by‑side task timelines showing failures without episodic memory and successes with Chameleon
Memory schematic: diagram of stored episodic traces (images + actions + outcomes) and the learned retrieval pipeline highlighting decision‑relevant matching
Flowchart: current observation -> episodic retrieval -> integrated policy -> action, showing how memory resolves ambiguity
Performance chart: success rate or cumulative reward over horizon length comparing baseline memory schemes vs Chameleon
paper_title: Chameleon: Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
paper_authors: Xinying Guo, Chenxi Jiang, Hyun Bin Kim, Ying Sun, Yang Xiao
